Desktop publishers focus on page production and final output quality. Managers direct priorities, designers define broader visual concepts, editors shape content, and production support roles maintain workflows. The differences lie in deliverables and accountability, not a simple hierarchy.

AI will not replace the occupation as a whole, but it will automate many structured tasks. People retain visual judgment, final review, and coordination. Professional depth and production judgment remain the main defenses against displacement (AI exposure 7/10).

Many employers value a relevant degree or production training, but career changers can enter through editing, design, print production, or project work. A strong portfolio, software fluency, and reliable production results can matter more than a single educational route.

A good fit for people with solid expertise, care for detail, the ability to judge under uncertainty, and a habit of continuous learning. Approach with caution if you avoid accountability, dislike repetitive process work, or resist updating your methods.
